job.title: Forward Deployed Engineer - New York City
job.description:
Forward Deployed Engineer - NYC 
 
Competitive base, uncapped upside tied to what you ship.
 
Working for our client, strategists scope and prioritize the bets.  Forward Deployed Engineers make them real.  You are the engineer who walks into a client codebase and ships the AI workflow that changes how thousands of people do their job.

You work close to the problem and close to the client. Architecture decisions are yours. The code is yours. The credit and the consequences are yours. You partner with Strategists to choose the right bets, with client engineering teams to ship inside their stack, and with the latest agentic coding tools to move at speeds that were not possible a year ago. The bar is production, not demos: what counts is the workflow running on Monday morning when nobody from the company is in the room.

Live engagements, to give a sense of the work:

- Insurance: an agent handling tier-1 claims disputes inside a fifteen-year-old claims platform for a national insurer, cutting resolution time for real  policyholders.

- Healthcare: an AI routing layer designed, prototyped with Claude, and rolled out across a three-hospital health system with the client's own engineers.

- Private equity: an agentic copilot over every portfolio company, built v1 to production by a single FDE and iterated with the team that uses it daily.

What you'll do:
- Own features end to end: architecture, implementation, deploy, and the relationship with client engineer reviewing your PR. Nothing gets handed off.
- Use every agentic coding tool that gives you leverage: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, whatever ships next week. Your throughput is measured and your pay scales with it.
- Ramp into unfamiliar codebases, from Fortune 500 monoliths in languages you have not touched in years to stacks built last quarter, without hand holding.
- Design agent systems that are reliable, auditable, and keep humans in the loop where they belong.
- Make the team better: workflow refinements from one engagement get adopted across every other engagement, so individual wins compound firm-wide.
 
What you MUST bring:
- 3 to 8 years building and shipping production software end to end, with a track record of turning complex problems into clean, scalable systems.
- AI as a core part of how you work: agentic coding tools raise the quality and throughput of everything you ship.
- Intellectual curiosity and range: you track new models, tools, and techniques and bring what you learn back to the team.
- Operational discipline: parallel workstreams across multiple clients without losing clarity or quality.
- Collaborative rigor: high standards for yourself and others, active contribution to team knowledge.
- Bonus: public artifacts (open source, a side project people use, a talk or post on applied AI engineering) and experience shipping a production agentic system end to end, not a POC.
 
Compensation, Benefits & Logistics
- $180k upwards with quarterly bonus. Structure: guaranteed base plus uncapped quarterly cash variable tied directly to output (typically $10k to $15k, much higher for top performers. 

- Benefits: comprehensive medical (PPO and HSA options), dental, vision, HSA and FSA, commuter benefits, 100% employer-paid life and AD&D, 100% employer-paid long-term disability, and responsible PTO.

- Workplace: in person from the NYC office five days a week, with travel to client sites roughly monthly. No relocation package, but non-local candidates willing to move to NYC are welcome.
 
Apply today with your resume for a confidential discussion.

Introduction
 
The Cyber and Digital Transformation Division (CDT) oversees all aspects of cyber and digital transformation across the entire NATO enterprise and is the principal institutional engine for advancing the Alliance's agenda on those issues. The division also coordinates on all aspects linked to countering hybrid actions. As a fully integrated civilian-military Division, it combines the strategic insight of the International Staff (IS) with the operational expertise of the International Military Staff (IMS), enabling coherent, credible, and actionable advice to NATO's senior decision-making bodies.
The Cyber Plans and Capabilities Section (CYPCAP) delivers technical and capability expertise in the field of cyber defense, cyber security, and cyber operations. Through the DPC substructure, the Section delivers technical and implementation directives on cyber security and cryptographic standards. The Section supports the Military Committee in its governance role for cryptographic modernization and transformation as well as in cyber matters. The Section also enables the operationalization of cyber as a domain through delivering cyber defense subject matter expertise into the NATO Defense Planning Process and the Common Funded Capability Delivery Governance Model. CYPCAP also oversees the implementation of the Cyber Adaptation Roadmap. Additionally, this section supports the Cyber Strategy and Policy Section in developing operational doctrine in cyberspace.
 
Objective
 
Specialist Public Key Infrastructure will play a role in all of activities related to Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and broader cryptography in CYPCAP. S/He will be responsible for preparation of draft policies, guidance and technical documentation related to NATO PKI. This specific task will require frequent engagement with various stakeholders possessing different backgrounds, therefore it is critical that the incumbent is able to clearly communicate and engage at an appropriate level.
S/He will support various activities related to ongoing NATO PKI projects, including analyzing architectures and designs, conducting feasibility assessment of project proposals, tracking delivery of projects and conducting audits of existing systems. All of the activities need to be properly documented. The incumbent will also be involved in risk management process related to NATO PKI activities
S/He might be required to engage with industry to gather best practices, conduct market surveys and analyse possible solution for inclusion into the NATO CIS ecosystem.
Additionally, S/He will support various cryptographic communities of interest through organizing meetings, coordinating attendance, supporting the local organizing entities and finally preparing and staffing meeting records. This will include managing NATO portals and supporting both internal and national representatives.
 
Tasks
 
The incumbent must be able to perform effectively and efficiently with minimal supervision the tasks described below.
  • Prepare draft documents related to NATO cryptography with focus on Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) and coordinate their approval through dedicated Working Groups and Committees.
  • Provide expertise in the field of cryptography (including post-quantum cryptography) and PKI in support of ongoing NATO and national initiatives.
  • Manage organization of events and develop records of the meetings.
  • Act as a secretary or staff support for different working groups.
  • Support conducting audits of systems and entities within the Organization.
  • Prepare presentations, speeches and speaking notes for senior officials as directed.
  • Provide continuous and quality executive advice to the Staff Officers on the relationship with the NATO cryptographic stakeholders.
  • Manage the cryptographic communities of interest portals and support external engagement.
Requirements
The candidate must meet the following requirements:
  • A university degree in Computer or Communication Science, Information Management, Information Security, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience (5+ years) in post-related field.
  • Possess comprehensive knowledge of the principles network security and symmetric and asymmetric cryptography; including quantum threat to cryptography.
  • Has very good understanding of PKI, including applicable RFCs and other standards, backed with practical implementation experience and/or experience in drafting PKI regulatory frameworks.
  • It is desirable that the contractor has previous experience with NATO-related cryptographic issues, such as the use of Type A algorithms, symmetric key distribution in a military environment and NATO policies on cryptography and cryptography procurement.
  • Possess experience in audit procedures, audit execution and post-audit remediation planning.
  • Demonstrate experience with risk management, as applied to cryptographic and/or cyber security fields.
  • Knowledge of NATO's internal structures, decision-making processes, stakeholder environment and civil-military working practices, gained through relevant professional experience is desirable.
  • Excellent written and spoken English (SLP 4343+), with the ability to communicate complex technical and policy issues clearly to a range of stakeholders.
  • The contractor must have proven communication and negotiation skills matured within a large international environment.
